chapter.heading: For Jeduthun, the music director. A psalm of Asaph.
chapter.v:
I cry
out to God for help—I even shout. If only he would listen to me!

When I
was in trouble I prayed to the Lord. All night long I stretched out my hands to him in prayer but nothing brought me any comfort.

I thought
about God, groaning loudly; I meditated on him, but I was discouraged. Selah.

You stop
me going to sleep; I'm so upset I can't even talk.

I think
of the old days, years ago.

I remember
the songs I sang in the night. I meditate and ask myself:

Has the
Lord given up on me forever? Won't he ever be pleased with me again?

Has his
trustworthy love disappeared forever? Have his promises permanently ended?

Has God
forgotten to be kind? Has he angrily slammed the door shut on his compassion? Selah.

Then I
said, “This is what hurts me the most: the Most High doesn't treat me the way he used to.”

I remember
what you have done, Lord; I remember all the wonderful things you did long ago.

I will
think about all you have accomplished; I will think deeply about how you have acted.

God, your
ways are holy; is any god as great as you?

You are
the God who does wonderful things! You have revealed your power to the nations.

Through your
strength you saved your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.

When the
waters saw you, God, when they looked they trembled! Yes, they shook down to the very depths!

The clouds
poured rain down; the skies crashed with thunder; your lightning flew like arrows.

Your thunder
rumbled from the whirlwind; lightning flashes lit up the world; the earth quaked and shook.

Your way
led through the sea; your path passed through the deep sea; yet your footprints were invisible.

You led
your people like a flock, shepherded by Moses and Aaron.
